recent_posts.title: Extending Your Enterprise Design System with a Product Library
recent_posts.summary: When design teams scale across multiple Scrum teams, consistency breaks down without a shared reference layer. A product library sits between the enterprise design system and day-to-day work, inheriting tokens and core components from the enterprise system while adding product-specific patterns, page templates, and status indicators. Built in Figma, it gives designers visibility into what exists, what is in progress, and what is finalized — eliminating duplicate work, accelerating onboarding, and keeping all teams aligned. The key is maintaining a two-way relationship with the enterprise system through design system champions, shared critiques, and inherited tokens that are never copied or overridden locally.

recent_posts.title: Building Prototypes Faster: AI Tools for Designers (Figma Make, Cursor, & Claude Code)
recent_posts.summary: Explores how AI tools like Figma Make, Cursor, and Claude Code can automate the tedious parts of prototyping, specifically connecting interactions and creating animations. Walks through a practical example of building an Instacart search prototype using Figma Make, covering setup, prompting strategies, and iterative refinement. Discusses real limitations including inconsistent results, poor mobile support, and unknown code quality, while identifying valuable use cases for stakeholder presentations, developer communication, and user testing.

recent_posts.title: How Designers Can Gather Better Feedback from Teams and Stakeholders
recent_posts.summary: Designers need structured approaches to gather meaningful feedback from different stakeholders throughout the design process. The article outlines specific strategies for collecting input from immediate teammates, cross-functional scrum teams, and executives. Key recommendations include using Loom videos for detailed team feedback, FigJam boards for cross-team collaboration, and silent QuickTime demos for busy executives. The focus is on matching communication methods to audience needs, establishing regular feedback rhythms, and seeking input early and often to prevent misalignment.

recent_posts.title: When Designers Should Build a Custom Design System from Scratch
recent_posts.summary: Designers may consider building a custom design system when industry-specific needs, large team scalability, and brand identity drive the need for complete control. Before embarking on such a project, it's crucial to have team and engineering support, a documented product roadmap, and a clear governance structure. Building a system involves phased implementation, collaboration between design and engineering, and ongoing measurement of success through metrics like business impact and team efficiency.

recent_posts.title: Design System Stakeholder Guide: Translating Progress into Business Value
recent_posts.summary: Learn how to effectively communicate the value of your design system to stakeholders using actionable strategies. The guide emphasizes the importance of aligning design system work with organizational goals, maintaining a living roadmap, establishing momentum-driving rituals, and providing comprehensive documentation. Proactive communication and stakeholder engagement are key to gaining recognition and support for your design system efforts.

recent_posts.title: App Mapping: Creating User Flows from Customer Journey Maps
recent_posts.summary: App mapping emphasizes the design of a product's flow, focusing on data relationships and structural clarity over visual design. It helps teams align on vision and goals, iterate quickly, and avoid costly rework. The process is distinct from customer journey mapping, which focuses on the user's experience. App mapping benefits designers, product owners, and developers by fostering collaboration, improving estimate accuracy, and providing a clear roadmap for development.

recent_posts.title: Taming `schema.rb` Chaos: A Rails Developer's Guide to Deterministic Schema Generation
recent_posts.summary: Rails 8.0.x will introduce deterministic schema generation to address `schema.rb` merge conflicts, enabling consistent ordering of tables, columns, and foreign keys. This change resolves merge conflicts, streamlines code reviews, and boosts productivity. Implementing a monkey patch allows developers to benefit from this feature today.

recent_posts.title: Migrating a React Native App to Expo
recent_posts.summary: Learn how to migrate your existing React Native app to Expo to utilize powerful features like over-the-air updates, push notifications, and seamless app store deployment. Understand the managed and bare workflows, assess your current project including native libraries and device features, and follow a step-by-step guide for migration. Additionally, get insights on configuring Expo Application Services for building, submitting, updating, and pushing notifications, along with essential QA/testing practices.

recent_posts.title: How to Tame Third-Party Packages with patch-package
recent_posts.summary: Solving issues with third-party packages can be challenging, but patch-package offers a viable solution. This powerful tool allows developers to apply necessary fixes or features to packages immediately after installation, ensuring smoother operations without waiting for official updates. Through an example involving a React Native issue, the steps to install and use patch-package are outlined, emphasizing its ability to manage temporary fixes efficiently. The post underscores the importance of treating patches as interim solutions while working towards long-term stability.

recent_posts.title: Dev Crit: Fostering a Culture of Growth in Software Development Teams
recent_posts.summary: Dev Crit is a structured process inspired by design critique, where developers present and receive feedback on their work to improve functionality, performance, scalability, and maintainability. It emphasizes creating a collaborative and trusting environment for constructive feedback, enabling personal and team growth. Headway has successfully implemented Dev Crit, fostering better collaboration and continuous improvement among its development team.

top_posts.title: VSCode Profiles: Optimize Your Coding Environment
top_posts.summary: Profiles are a useful feature in VSCode that allow you to save and switch between different sets of preferences and configurations. For a React front-end project, you might want to install extensions such as Ruby and Solargraph. Profiles let you create workspaces with unique configurations and preferences for each project or task.

top_posts.title: TypeScript Generics Explained - Creating Reusable Components
top_posts.summary: TypeScript has a few ways to refactor and reuse common types. The one we’re going to cover today is generics. A TS generic is a concept borrowed from other more strongly typed languages. It allows a component to work across a variety of types, rather than a single one.

top_posts.title: Design to Code: The Role of Atomic Design in Front-End Development
top_posts.summary: " atomic design" is a methodology for designing and building user interfaces in a systematic and structured way. The methodology was created by Brad Frost and is based on the idea that complex user interfaces can be broken down into smaller, more manageable parts or building blocks. Using atomic design, designers and developers can create a more efficient and cohesive design process.

top_posts.title: Custom React Hooks with useHug
top_posts.summary: Building custom hooks is a great way to encapsulate behaviors and reuse them throughout your application. To demonstrate this, we're going to build out the idea of "hugging" elements of our UI. Our huggable behavior will: Change the mouse cursor on hover (we want our user to know what needs a hug) Scale the element down on click (this is a firm hug, some squishiness is expected) Change the cursor while clicking (to show our appreciation)
